reviewMethod: Model-blind view_image inspection of every available decoded frame covering each of the six original proposed contact spans, including the immediately preceding/following boundary frames. New sequential OpenCV decode with one active CPU decoder/one decoder thread and cv2.setNumThreads(1), verified against hash-pinned original FFmpeg integer PTS and its +3ms OpenCV offset. All prior saved all-frame contact sheets also re-inspected. Chronological still-frame inspection; no real-time video playback, no FPS-derived clocks, no audio/model scores/inference/training/GPU/downloads.
limitations: Provisional assistant judgments, not human ground truth or independent human review.
Sport/practice/instructional contact proxies do not establish real hostile fights, intent, force, injury, identity, guilt or crime.
Every available decoded frame was inspected; motion between video exposures and native PTS gaps is not directly observed. Native gaps are explicitly recorded; no frame/time synthesis.
Contact evidence establishes a scene-level episode, not exhaustive localization or labeling of every person/pair in the frame. Tokyo contains partial occlusion of other pairs.
Only the proposed 39 seconds are adjudicated here; all other source time remains outside this dense review and is never newly marked normal.
Original source groups/roles are unchanged. Actor/session independence and publisher/pretraining overlap remain unknown. This adds no independent recordings or human ground truth.
Original source rights/participant-release limitations remain as recorded in the original bundle; no new clearance or camera/night/crowd capability is asserted.
